problems.title: Minimum of a radical fraction
problems.question: Find the minimum of f(x)=3−2/[2+√(x−5)].
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The domain is x≥5. The denominator is at least2, so the subtracted fraction is at most1.
steps: Thus f(x)≥2, with equality at x=5.

problems.title: Largest negative progression term
problems.question: An arithmetic progression has a₁=7.5, d=−0.3. Find its largest negative term.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
steps: At n=26, it is 0; at n=27, it is −0.3. Later terms are more negative.

problems.title: Multiply conjugate nested radicals
problems.question: Evaluate⁸√(√3+√2)·¹⁶√(5−2√6).
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
steps: The second factor is⁸√(√3−√2). Their product is⁸√[(√3+√2)(√3−√2)]=⁸√1=1.

problems.title: Polygon angle from its diagonal count
problems.question: A regular polygon has 20 diagonals. Find an interior angle.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
steps: Interior angle=(n−2)180°/n=135°.

problems.title: Rhombus area from inradius and a diagonal
problems.question: A rhombus has inradius3 and larger diagonal12. Find are a.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Let half the smaller diagonal be v. Side=√(36+v²), are a=12v. Also are a=inradius×semiperimeter=6√(36+v²).
steps: Equate and square:4v²=36+v², so v²=12, v=2√3. Area=24√3.

problems.title: First eight geometric terms
problems.question: cₙ=5·2ⁿ, n≥1. Find c₁+…+c₈.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The geometric sum 2+4+…+256=2⁹−2=510.
steps: Multiply by 5 to obtain2550.

problems.title: Order four powers of two
problems.question: Order a=16^(1/5), b=4^(1/3), c=⁷√32, d=⁷√64.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The base2 exponents are 4/5,2/3,5/7,6/7.
steps: Since 2/3<5/7<4/5<6/7, the increasing order is b, c, a, d.

problems.title: Fractional part of a telescoping sum
problems.question: Find the fractional part of 1/(1·2)+1/(2·3)+…+1/(19·20).
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
steps: The sum telescopes to 1−1/20=19/20, already between0 and 1. Its fractional part is 0.95.

problems.title: Three unit vectors sum to zero
problems.question: Three planar vectors sum to 0, and each pairwise-sum magnitude is 1. Find the common angle between pairs.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Each pairwise sum equals the negative of the remaining vector, so all 3 vectors have magnitude1.
steps: For any pair,1=|a+b|²=1+1+2cosθ. Thus cosθ=−1/2, so θ=120°.

problems.title: A zero dot product
problems.question: Find n if(n+1,3−n) is perpendicular to(5,7).
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
steps: This simplifies to 26−2n=0, n=13.

problems.title: A geometric-progression minimum
problems.question: A geometric progression has b₇=12. Minimize b₁₇/b₁₅−6b₁₁/b₁₀+b₇.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Let the common ratio be r≠0. The expression is r²−6r+12=(r−3)²+3.
steps: Its minimum 3 is attained at r=3, a valid ratio.

problems.title: A listed congruence root
problems.question: Which listed x satisfies12x≡39(mod 15)?
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Divide by 3:4x≡13(mod 5), so x≡2(mod 5).
steps: Among13,18,25,29,32,41, only 32 has remainder2 modulo5.

problems.title: A radical-product inequality
problems.question: Count integers satisfying(x²−12x+27)√(x²−7x+10)≤0.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The radical domain is x≤2 or x≥5. Its zeros2,5 are automatically solutions. Away from them, the polynomial(x−3)(x−9) must be≤0.
steps: Intersecting[3,9] with the domain gives[5,9]. Add the isolated root 2.
The integers are 2,5,6,7,8,9:6 values.

problems.title: Uniform point in an annular sector
problems.question: Concentric circles have radii8,6. A point is uniform in the larger disk. Find its probability of landing in the 60° annular sector.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Favourable are a=(60/360)π(8²−6²). Total are a=64π.
steps: The ratio is 28/(6·64)=7/96.

problems.title: Squared distances from square vertices to a central line
problems.question: A square side is 2. Find the sum of squared vertex distances to any line through its centre.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Place vertices at(±1,±1). Let a unit normal to the line be(u, v), u²+v²=1.
steps: The 4 squared signed distances sum to(u+v)²+(u−v)²+(−u+v)²+(−u−v)²=4(u²+v²)=4.

problems.title: Minimum of a composite quadratic
problems.question: g(x)=x², f(x)=2x−1. Find the minimum of 2f(x)+f(g(x)).
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The expression is 2(2x−1)+(2x²−1)=2(x+1)²−5.
steps: The minimum is −5, at x=−1.

problems.title: A squared numerator over a variable denominator
problems.question: Solve1/(5x−x²−4)+5x−x²−6≥0.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Put t=5x−x²−4≠0. The expression is 1/t+t−2=(t−1)²/t.
steps: It is nonnegative exactly when t>0. Thus 5x−x²−4>0, or(x−1)(x−4)<0.

problems.title: Probability of at least one man
problems.question: Choose4 delegates uniformly from 5 women,3 men. Find probability of at least one man.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Use the complement of an all-women delegation:1−C(5,4)/C(8,4).
steps: The result is 1−5/70=13/14.

problems.title: Foot of a perpendicular gives tangency
problems.question: A circle centre(3,−2), radius √10, touches y=−x/3+7/3. Find the sum of contact coordinates.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: The line is x+3y−7=0, normal(1,3). The centre residual is 3−6−7=−10, and the normal squared length is 10.
steps: The perpendicular foot is(3,−2)−(−10/10)(1,3)=(4,1). The coordinate sum is 5.

problems.title: Dot products of regular-hexagon edge vectors
problems.question: For regular ABCDEF, find(AB·BC)/(BC·DE).
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Consecutive directed edges differ by 60°, so AB·BC=s²cos60°=s²/2. Edges BC, DE differ by 120°.
steps: Their dot product is −s²/2. The quotient is −1.

problems.title: A listed mode-median sum
problems.question: Natural data a, b, c, d,7,2,9 have mode2 below the median. Which listed sum can occur?
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: If median=t, mode=t−2, their sum is 2t−2 and must be even.
steps: Sums14,18,20 would put the repeated mode plus the fixed smaller entries below the proposed median too often, so they are impossible.
Sum6 works:the data2,2,3,4,7,8,9 have unique mode2 and median4.

problems.title: Exactly two tourists in one carriage
problems.question: Three tourists independently choose uniformly among4 train carriages. Find probability exactly 2 share a carriage.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Total assignments=4³=64. Choose the sharing pair in C(3,2)=3 ways, their carriage in4 ways, and the third’s different carriage in3 ways.
steps: Favourable assignments=3·4·3=36. Probability36/64=9/16.

problems.title: Three roots of an absolute-value parabola
problems.question: For which listed a does|x²−6x+5|=a have exactly 3 real roots?
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Write|(x−3)²−4|=a. The critical nonnegative level is a=4.
steps: At a=4, the inner equation equal to −4 gives x=3 once, and the inner equation equal to 4 gives x=3±√8.
Thus there are 3 distinct roots. Other positive levels below4 give4 roots, and levels above4 give2.

problems.title: Rectangle in a45° sector
problems.question: A45° sector has radius 2√5. Rectangle FEMN has FE on OA, N on OB, M on the arc, and FE=2FN. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Let FN=h, FE=2h and OA horizontal. Since N lies on the 45° ray, the near x-coordinate is h. The far upper vertex is M=(3h, h).
steps: The circle condition gives 10h²=(2√5)²=20, so h=√2. Perimeter=2(2h+h)=6√2.

problems.title: Outward normal vectors of a polygon
problems.question: From an interior point, draw outward normals toward the 5 side lines of a convex pentagon, with lengths equal to the corresponding side lengths 5,6,5,9,9. Find the magnitude of their sum.
problems.idea: Use exact substitutions, complements, and vector identities; retain the original domain.
formulas: Orient the polygon edges consistently around its boundary. Their vector sum is 0 because the path closes.
steps: Rotating every edge by the same90° gives the outward normal vectors with the prescribed lengths. Rotation preserves vector addition, so their sum is also0.
